entries.action: the hawkish repricing is holding, but the transmission channel matters
entries.rationale: Rate markets have settled around a 60% chance of a September HIKE, from roughly the inverse before the keynote. The framing worth carrying into the week: bitcoin does not respond much to the September decision itself - it responds to global liquidity and to where the LONG END settles, which is the same channel that drives gold. That is exactly what Friday demonstrated, when the 30-year rallied 2bp on a hawkish speech while the 2-year rose 6bp. So the thing to watch through September is the long end and the Sept 9 buyback start, not the FOMC odds headline. One claim I am NOT repeating as fact: some coverage says the record $2.6bn ETF inflow week has 'now reversed' post-Warsh, but the sourcing is ambiguous and one headline appears to be from an older article. The Friday flow print is the datapoint that would settle it and it was not yet published at snapshot time.

entries.action: SERIOUS DATA FAULT - I have been rating a DELISTED stock as a live BUY for four weeks

Abu Dhabi Power Corporation, which held 98.12%, compulsorily acquired the remaining shares; the Abu Dhabi Depository verified 100% ownership on August 13 and the board resolved to delist on August 25. The takeover was by L'imad - the same sovereign vehicle now bidding for AD Ports. My engine kept rating it BUY (+25) on the identical 2.66 print, with the identical -0.37% change, EVERY DAY from at least Aug 5 through Sept 1 - 27 consecutive runs - and it appeared on the UAE shortlist that whole time. The fetch log said OK every one of those days. That is the defect: my guards catch MISSING data and ABSURD data, but nothing caught FROZEN data, because the source kept serving a delisted instrument's last-ever print and the fetch genuinely succeeded. The failure that started Sept 1 was not the bug; it was the bug finally becoming visible. Had Al Ramz been open, TAQA would have been on the shortlist as a buy candidate for a stock that cannot be bought.

entries.action: frozen-quote guard added, calibrated from real data
entries.rationale: The engine now counts consecutive identical closes per asset and flips the signal to STALE DATA with a score of 0 once the count passes a threshold, suppressing its alerts the same way INSUFFICIENT DATA does. The thresholds are calibrated from 30 runs of this book's own history rather than guessed: live UAE stocks legitimately repeat a close up to SEVEN times, because the daily snapshots repeat the last close across weekends and holidays, so the stock threshold is 10. Crypto trades continuously, where three identical closes is already unambiguous, so that threshold is 3. Verified both ways - a stock with 8 identical closes stays rated, a stock with 12 flips to STALE DATA, crypto flips at 4, and any moving price resets the counter to zero. At a 10-run threshold TAQA would have been caught around Aug 16 rather than Sept 2. That is 17 days late in this instance, but it is the right threshold given the weekend-repeat noise, and the stale_runs count is now emitted so a rising number is visible before it trips.
